label: Children with Disabilities
definition: Share of civilian noninstitutionalized children under 18 with a hearing, vision, cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, or independent living difficulty.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table DP02)

label: Young Children (Under Age 5 Share of Kids)
definition: Children under age 5 as a share of all children under 18.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table S0101)

label: Children (5-17) in Limited English Speaking Households
definition: Share of children ages 5 to 17 living in households where no one age 14 or older speaks only English or speaks English "very well."
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Tables B16003, B16004)

label: Foreign-Born Children
definition: Share of children under 18 who were not U.S. citizens at birth (born outside the U.S. to non-citizen parents).
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Tables B05003, S0101)

label: Children in Immigrant Families
definition: Share of own children under 18 in families who live with at least one foreign-born parent. Most of these children are U.S.-born citizens.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B05009)

label: Children in Single-Parent Households
definition: Share of own children under 18 in families who live with a single parent (male or female householder, no spouse present).
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B09002)

label: Projected Child Share of Population, 2060
definition: Projected children under 18 as a share of the total population in 2060 (mid migration scenario).
source: Texas Demographic Center (TDC), 2024 Population Projections (Mid Scenario)

label: Children in Poverty (<100% FPL)
definition: Share of children under 18 (for whom poverty status is determined) living in families with incomes below 100% of the federal poverty level.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table S1701)

label: Children in Extreme Poverty (<50% FPL)
definition: Share of children under 18 (for whom poverty status is determined) living in families with incomes below 50% of the federal poverty level.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B17024)

label: Low-Income Children (<200% FPL)
definition: Share of children under 18 (for whom poverty status is determined) living in families with incomes below 200% of the federal poverty level.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B17024)

label: Children with No Parent in the Labor Force
definition: Share of own children under 18 in families whose resident parent(s) are not in the labor force (neither working nor looking for work).
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B23008)

label: Households with Children Receiving SNAP
definition: Share of households with children under 18 that received SNAP (food stamp) benefits in the past 12 months.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B22002)

label: Child Food Insecurity
definition: Estimated share of children under 18 living in food-insecure households, 2024.
source: Feeding America, Map the Meal Gap 2026 (2024 data)

label: Uninsured Children (Under 19)
definition: Share of civilian noninstitutionalized children under 19 with no health insurance coverage.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table S2701)

label: Late or No Prenatal Care
definition: Share of 2024 live births where prenatal care began after the first trimester or not at all. 2024 DSHS data are provisional and subject to change.
source: Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS), Center for Health Statistics, 2024 Live Birth File (provisional)
us_note: U.S. value is from a different source: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), Births: Final Data for 2024.

label: Children Without Home Internet Access
definition: Share of children under 18 in households that have a computer but no internet subscription.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B28005)

label: Public Pre-K Enrollment (Ages 3-4)
definition: Public school Pre-K enrollment in fall 2025 as a share of children ages 3 and 4 (2020-2024 ACS average).
note: County rates include charter schools, counted in the county where the charter is based. School district rates include only the district's own schools, not charters, so districts where many families use charter Pre-K will look lower than reality. Students are counted where they enroll, which may not be where they live. The margin of error reflects only the ACS estimate of children ages 3 and 4.
source: Texas Education Agency (TEA), PEIMS Student Enrollment, 2025-26; U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B09001)
missing_note: No data: TEA masked a small Pre-K count, the rate is over 100% (the area enrolls children who live elsewhere), or no school district is based here
us_note: U.S. value is from a different source and year: National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), share of 3- and 4-year-olds enrolled in public preschool or kindergarten programs, 2023 (Current Population Survey), as reported by USAFacts. It is survey-based and counts children by where they live, not school enrollment records.
unreliable_note: Not shown: the ACS estimate of children ages 3-4 (the denominator) is unreliable (CV > 40%)

label: Teens (16-19) Not in School and Not Working
definition: Share of teens ages 16 to 19 who are not enrolled in school and are not working (unemployed or not in the labor force), whether or not they finished high school.
source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 American Community Survey (ACS) 5-Year Estimates (Table B14005)

label: High School Graduation Rate (4-Year)
definition: Share of the class of 2025 (students who began grade 9 in 2021-22) who graduated within four years.
source: Texas Education Agency (TEA), Four-Year Longitudinal Graduation Rates, Class of 2025
missing_note: Masked by TEA for student privacy, or no graduating class
us_note: U.S. value is from a different source and year: National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), EDFacts, 4-year adjusted cohort graduation rate, 2022-23 school year (latest available), as reported by America's Health Rankings. It uses the same federal definition as the TEA rate.
